reason: The bearing frames should support the rotating shaft on the mechanism base.
expectation: The frames will fit onto the base to support the crankshaft.

effect: The bearing frames are installed, so the base is ready for a shaft.
reaction: That was the expected first fitting.
reason: The crankshaft belongs in the newly installed shaft bearings.
expectation: The crankshaft will fit into the bearings and turn on the base.

effect: The crankshaft is installed, giving the cam a rotating shaft to attach to.
reaction: The shaft fitting worked as expected.
reason: The off-centre cam should mount on the crankshaft to turn rotation into a lifting motion.
expectation: The cam will fit onto the crankshaft and turn with it.

effect: The cam is installed, and its off-centre edge changes height as the shaft turns.
reaction: The comparison with a centred disc makes the lifting mechanism clearer.
reason: The follower guide should provide a controlled path for the rod above the cam.
expectation: The guide will attach to the mechanism so the follower rod can move up and down.

effect: The rod must be fitted into its guide before the assembly joins the mechanism; that happened automatically.
reaction: I expected to attach the guide first, so the assembly order was a small surprise.
reason: The guided follower should sit above the cam so its changing height can lift the rod.
expectation: The guided follower will attach above the cam.

effect: The guided follower is now positioned over the cam; the spring and handle remain to be fitted.
reaction: The assembly went together as expected.
reason: The follower spring should keep the rod in contact with the cam as it turns.
expectation: The spring will fit onto the follower mechanism and help it follow the cam down as well as up.

effect: The spring is fitted, and the mechanism invites a comparison with an unhooked run when tested.
reaction: I am curious how much difference the spring makes.
reason: The removable crank handle should let me turn and test the assembled lifter.
expectation: The handle will attach to the shaft so the cam and follower can be tested.

effect: The test confirmed that the spring keeps the follower against the cam on the downward stroke, completing the lifter.
reaction: The comparison made the spring’s purpose satisfying and clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting and testing the spring was most worthwhile: the comparison showed why the follower needs a gentle pull to track the cam reliably.

leastWorthwhile.text: Installing the bearing frames was straightforward setup, with less to discover than the later mechanism test.

surprise.text: I expected the guide to attach to the mechanism first, but the rod needed to go into it before the assembly could be fitted.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; even the unexpected assembly order had a clear result.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the lifter makes the paper dragon wave; learning how the cam and spring work was worth the time.
